key_insight: Stochastic Neumann inverse-Hessian estimates can amplify skewness, while antithetic pairing cancels all odd-order noise terms when the reference Hessian is exact.
engineering_relevance: More reliable hypergradients can improve bilevel workflows such as hyperparameter tuning and data reweighting on noisy, heterogeneous, or imbalanced datasets.
method: Pair each sampled Hessian with its mirror around a reference Hessian.
Average the paired Neumann inverse-Hessian estimates to cancel odd-order perturbations.
Integrate the modified Hessian-vector step into ANE-SGD or recursively variance-reduced ANE-VR.
evidence_signal: Across four task families with 20 seeds each, ANE-based methods report 4–25% lower loss than the best baseline, including 25% lower test loss and 54% higher test R-squared on robust regression.
watch_item: Exact odd-order cancellation requires an exact reference Hessian; with an approximate reference, residual odd-order contributions are bounded linearly in the reference error.
paper_title: Your Hypergradient is Skewed: Antithetic Neumann Estimation for Bilevel Optimization
